notes:
- The info page is one scroll, not three tabs: A title's details opened on three tabs - Story, Specs and My Entry - which split one title's information across two of them: the synopsis on one, the numbers on the other, and no way to see both without switching between them. They are now a single page that scrolls: artwork, watching progress, synopsis, production details, genres, tags, the cast, the crew, the other titles in the franchise, and the things you can do with it. Only editing still has a place of its own, reached from the capsule at the bottom of the page, because editing is a mode rather than a section of it.
- A title now says who made it: The details screen asked AniList for a show's numbers but never for its people. It now asks for the cast with their voice actors, the crew with the position each one held, and the rest of the franchise. Characters are shown with the voice actor beside them, staff portraits carry the job they did - Original Creator, Chief Director - and related titles are labelled with how they relate, filtered to anime so the light novel a show was adapted from or its guidebook does not appear in a row of sequels.
- The progress bar fills as a wave: Watching Progress was a ruled line. It is now a wave that rises as you get further in and travels while you are part-way through, drawn from the same measurement AniList reports, with the episode count beside it and a countdown when the next episode has a date. It fills once when the page opens, and the travelling stops on a title you have not started, so a screenful of untouched titles is not a screenful of loops. The motion style you picked in Settings decides how much of it moves: Instant draws it flat and still.
- The artwork moves out of the way as you scroll: The page opens on the show's key visual, blurred behind its own title, and that backdrop slides and grows more slowly than the page does, so the artwork stays behind the text instead of scrolling with it - and it dims as it goes rather than being clipped off at the top edge. The title lifts away against it while a docked bar drops in carrying the same title and the same two controls, so opening the title on AniList or closing the page works from anywhere on it. The cards below arrive in sequence rather than all at once, in the draw phase, so the entrance costs no layout work while the sheet is still settling.
- Production details read as a card, not a four-column grid: Studio, episodes, duration, season, status, format, source, score, popularity and the alternative titles were spread across a grid wide enough to wrap half of its values onto a second line on a phone. They are now two columns of label over value inside one card, with the studio named above them and every name the title goes by underneath. AniList's thematic tags carry the share of viewers who applied them - 'Urban Fantasy 96%' - rather than eight bare words with no weight to them.
- Stats are read in three views, not one long page: The genre table and the tag table are the two biggest things on the Stats tab - AniList tags an entry with everything it is - and both sat below the score, status, format, country, year and episode cards, so the answer to 'what do I actually watch' was three screens down with nothing on the page saying it was there. There is now a row of chips at the top: Overview, Genres and Tags, each carrying its own count, so you can tell whether a section has anything in it before opening it. The Overview keeps every distribution that is read in one pass.
- Followers and Following read as names as well as faces: The Social tab only showed portraits, and the name under each one was cut to a single ellipsised line - a handle like PotatoWithThoug... tells you nothing, and the search field cannot help with it because search needs the name. A button beside the search switches the grid to a list: one person per row, portrait beside the whole name. The grid is still what you get first, because recognising somebody is what it is for.
- The activity feed builds each row from a smaller picture: Every card in the activity feed blurs its cover behind itself, at about half strength, as a colour wash. That blur was being handed the card's own size - roughly a thousand pixels wide on a phone - and then smearing away every bit of that detail anyway. The backdrop is now decoded at a fraction of that, so each row costs less to put together as it scrolls into view. Nothing on screen changes: the blur was destroying that detail regardless.
- The Library tab remembers your filter and your sort: Switching to Activity and coming back reset the Library grid to 'All' in list order every single time, because the choice lived inside the tab and the tab is thrown away on every switch. The media type was already remembered; the status filter, the sort and the direction you sorted it in now are too, and all of them come back together so the grid never paints a half-restored selection.
- Opening a manga now loads that manga: The title page fetched its details by number alone, and AniList's numbers are unique per category rather than across all of them - anime/1 and manga/1 are two different titles. So opening a manga could answer with the anime sharing that number, showing its story, cast and relations; where no anime had that number, the request failed and the page quietly kept the thin summary from the list, with no cast, no crew and no relations at all. Manga now load properly wherever you open them from, and the cache keeps the two apart so one cannot be served in place of the other.
- You can walk a franchise from the title page: The row of related titles was decorative - the artwork could not be tapped, because a sheet opened from inside a sheet leaves you with no way back that you can see. Tapping a related title now replaces the page in place, so a prequel, a sequel or the rest of a series is one tap away, from any screen in the app, and the same page renders it in full. The page also starts at the top of the new title rather than inheriting where you were scrolled to on the last one.
- Fixed gaps and repeated text on the title page: Sections with nothing to show - no progress on a title you have not started, no crew, no relations, no alternative titles - left an empty 14dp hole in the page, because a list gives every section the same space whether or not it drew anything. They no longer take up room at all. Alternative Titles repeated the title the page already shows in full, which for most titles meant the same name printed twice; it now lists only the names the page is not already showing, and a title with just the one name no longer draws an empty card. 'Read more' on the story now appears whenever the story is actually cut off, not only when it is long enough by character count to be worth guessing at.
- Crew portraits stop pretending to be buttons: The crew portraits squashed when you touched them and then did nothing, which reads as a broken control rather than a decoration. They are still a row of artwork - the positions each person held are printed under them - but they no longer invite a tap that goes nowhere.
- The title page shows its artwork clearly: The artwork behind the title was blurred, which turned a poster into a smear of colour and made the page look worse the better the artwork was. It is now shown sharp, and the darkening behind the title was deepened to keep every word readable over it.
- Your profile groups the people you have pinned: Favourite Characters and Favourite Staff were two separate headings above two identical rows of portraits, which reads as two kinds of thing rather than as one list of people. They are one row under one heading now, a crew member without a listed job shows how many people pinned them instead of the word Staff, and an actor who appears both as a character voice and as staff appears once rather than twice.
- Opening your own profile from the dashboard works again: Tapping your avatar, or the profile button on the demo dashboard, did nothing at all: the profile is registered as a route with an optional tab argument, and the avatar navigated to that route without the argument, which matches no screen. It now lands on your profile as intended.
- Each profile remembers its own tab: Opening somebody elses profile from the Social tab landed you on whichever tab you had left your own profile on, because the tab was saved without knowing which profile it belonged to. Every profile now keeps its own tab, and a rotation still returns you to it.
- Facts read as facts: Studio, Episodes, Duration, Season and the rest were set in almost the same size and weight as the numbers under them, so the details card read as one block of text rather than as a list of labelled answers. Each label is now a small capital above its value, which is what makes a number findable when you are looking for one, and the pairs are spaced apart so a two-column grid no longer runs together as four columns.
- Bold text in a bio actually looks bold: Bold in an AniList bio rendered as body text very slightly heavier, which for most of a phone screen was impossible to tell apart from normal - and bios lean on bold hard, so whole lines meant to stand out were not. Bold is now a heavier weight, and underlined text is emphasised rather than underlined with a near-invisible hairline.
- Library posters say a little more: A poster told you its title and its progress and nothing else, so a grid of thirty was a wall of art you had to read one caption at a time. Each poster now carries its score or format on a quieter line underneath, and a title that already contains that text does not repeat it. Titles are capped to one line so the new line has room, and the poster image no longer announces the title that is printed directly below it.
- The title page stopped printing API names: A TV special read TV_SHORT and a one-shot manga read ONE_SHOT - AniList internal names with underscores, shown in the chip under the title and in the details grid beside Episodes and Season. Status had already been cleaned up years ago and format never was, so the two disagreed in the same card. Both now read as words, and the format filter still matches what you pick.
- The title stays readable over its own artwork: With the artwork no longer blurred, the title over it could fade into a pale poster. The title now carries its own shadow rather than the whole hero being darkened, so the words stay legible and the artwork stays as bright as it is drawn.

Regenerated from assets/changelog.json by hand, because this file is written by the release workflow and its commit back to main is refused by branch protection. The workflow overwrites it at publish time and fills in size_bytes and published_at, which cannot be known for a version that has not been built yet.
